cite_locations.context: For general CFLs, online recognition means reporting whether each observed prefix is a complete sentence, whereas TPC asks whether it has some extension after a candidate. Dudek and Gawrychowski give an \emph{upper} bound for the former in terms of OMv machinery~\cite{onlinecfg}; their title is not an OMv lower bound. Gallaire's earlier lower bound uses online Turing machines~\cite{gallaire}, not this RAM model. Sliding-window recognition can be OMv-hard even for a fixed deterministic real-time language~\cite{sliding}, but window deletion changes the update model. We do not import that lower bound into append-only decoding. Our construction supplies its own explicit grammar, stream, and candidate predicate.
